note: THE JOIN TABLE. A THEME binds the 4 independent vectors: Color, Typography, Forms, and Spacing -- and as of schemaVersion 4 it declares TWO colours, a primary and an alt, each by explicit slug. Apps reference a THEME slug and the resolver composes everything. An app that names ONE theme gets both of its colours as its light/dark toggle; an app that names a SECOND theme replaces the alt with that theme's primary colour. The app always owns which slot is which.

vocabulary.color: entity -- the PRIMARY palette, by slug, from vectors/colors.tsv.
vocabulary.alt-color: entity -- the palette the other toggle state uses, by slug. Usually the opposite mode, but NOT required to be: two darks or normal-and-party are equally legal, because nothing infers a relationship.
vocabulary.typography: entity -- fonts + size ramp + tracking. e.g. sharp-racing.
vocabulary.forms: entity -- tactility: radii, border weight, shadows, elevation, motion, gradient angle. sharp | soft | grounded.
vocabulary.spacing: entity -- density: touch target, padding, gaps. tight | standard | loose | flush | database.
vocabulary.theme: JOIN -- a named combination of two colours and one token from each remaining vector.

rules.pairing: Pairing lives HERE and ONLY here. vectors/colors.tsv carries no identity column, no alt- band, and no relationship of any kind -- it is a canonical object vector and it is clueless by design (Michael, 2026-08-05). There is no such thing as a theme family.
rules.dangling: Because the pair is a POINTER it can dangle, which a derived pair could not. A consumer MUST report an unresolvable slug by name and must never fall back silently -- that is the whole price of the expressiveness, paid openly.
rules.mode: A colour row's `mode` resolves nothing any more. It is descriptive, and it exists so a consumer can warn when a dark palette lands in a light slot. Keep it honest.
rules.typography-forms-spacing: These do NOT split by toggle state. Type is scheme-independent by design, and a radius or a cell padding has no business changing when a reader flips a switch. One theme supplies all three.

themes.name: Sharp Utility
themes.intendedUse: Tight instrument/data look -- the sleek dashboard direction (Retrocast).

themes.name: Soft Utility
themes.intendedUse: Balanced everyday default for new apps copied from template-app.

themes.name: Soft Racing · Mercedes
themes.intendedUse: soft-utility's feel with the Mercedes palette -- petronas teal accent on a near-black green-tinted ground, silver as the secondary. Built 2026-07-30 for inciardi-collection. A pure COLOR swap: typography/forms/spacing are byte-identical to soft-utility, so anything that reads correctly in one reads correctly in the other.

themes.name: Sharp Carbon
themes.intendedUse: Neutral-cool tight instrument look; alternative to sharp-utility.

themes.name: Database
themes.intendedUse: THE DATABASE LOOK (Michael, 2026-08-03) -- maximum row density, gaps collapsed, chrome out of the way. Named for the words he actually uses, so 'give me the database look' resolves in a grep, in this file and in the spacing grid. Deliberately `sharp-utility` with ONE pointer changed (spacing tight -> database) so the two are comparable and any difference is attributable to spacing alone. WARNING status DRAFT: composed but never rendered -- nothing has consumed it yet, so nobody has looked at it. Promote to locked only after it has been seen. WARNING SIBLING, NOT A RIVAL: the `flush` spacing row is the other dense option and it optimises a DIFFERENT axis -- flush hugs the viewport EDGE, database maximises ROWS. If nobody can state that difference on sight, retire one rather than letting both drift. WARNING the slug collides with the `database` spacing entity; a consumer must resolve a bare name as a JOIN first and report the ambiguity.

themes.name: On Track · Racing Bulls
themes.intendedUse: The On Track motorsport schedule -- navy+red Racing Bulls identity, Archivo display headers, rounded soft chrome. Series identity colors ride on top as a local layer (not theme tokens). WARNING 2026-08-01: the `red-bull` COLOR row's accent moved from red to the can's yellow (the board rework -- four teams were sharing one red). This theme's chrome accent therefore changed with it. If On Track wants the old red it is now `accent-2` on the same row, or it gets its own color entity -- do NOT add a local override.

themes.name: Eos
themes.intendedUse: Lighting/theatrical apps -- ETC Eos console grammar. Shared across the LX-notes clone, the Eos Tombstone Teaching Tool, and future lighting tools. THE SEMANTIC TOKENS ARE THE CONSOLE'S OWN GRAMMAR AND ARE NOT FREE TO RE-COLOUR: accent-2 magenta = tracked, info blue = intensity up, good green = lower/marked, warn gold = captured/selected, bad red = manual. A board op reads those five colours faster than they read a label, so changing one to taste breaks a language rather than a palette. The dark row's chrome is the console's blue-tinted charcoal in BLIND (re-authored 2026-08-05 from a photograph of an Element2, replacing a per-token identification harness that had served its purpose); every chrome cell sits within three degrees of hue 217. WARNING this slug exists as a join, a colour, a typography, a forms AND a spacing entity; a consumer must resolve a bare name as a JOIN first and report the ambiguity.

themes.name: F1 Racetracks
themes.intendedUse: THE f1-racetracks app's single point of entry to the theme system (Michael, 2026-08-01). Named for the app on purpose: it is an app identity, not a constructor palette, and no team owns violet. Every pointer reproduces what the app already renders, so adopting it is a swap of a hand-baked layer for one pointer rather than a restyle. WARNING Team colours are NOT in this join and must never be swept into one: a theme applies ONE AT A TIME, the standings matrix renders eleven teams AT ONCE (J14). They stay a local identity layer read from colors.tsv as data.

themes.name: Papyrus
themes.intendedUse: Warm editorial / HML LLC FileMaker renders and natural-light applications. Gabarito display, IBM Plex Mono, zero-radius base, subtle parchment shadows. NOTE this is the one join whose PRIMARY is light and whose alt is dark -- proof the pair carries no assumption about which way round it goes.
